subject.title: bug(telegram): reply to bot photo injects bot-sent media as inbound user attachment

question: Should Telegram reply-chain media hydration skip bot-authored reply targets, or is the current behavior of hydrating visible bot-authored reply media an intentional context feature?
rationale: Current source still allows bot-authored reply-chain media hydration when visibility allows it, while tests now assert that behavior; changing it would alter Telegram reply context semantics and should be owner-confirmed before automation writes a fix.

options.title: Skip bot-authored reply media
options.body: Land a current-main guard in `resolveReplyMediaForChain` and update focused tests so reply-chain text remains visible but bot-sent media is not reattached as inbound media.

options.title: Keep current hydration behavior
options.body: Treat visible bot-authored reply media as intentional reply context and close this issue with a maintainer explanation of why the agent may see its own prior media.

options.title: Narrow by chat or visibility mode
options.body: Define a more specific contract, such as skipping bot-authored media only for direct replies or only outside explicit visibility modes, then add tests for both sides.

recommendation.title: Skip bot-authored reply media
recommendation.body: Land a current-main guard in `resolveReplyMediaForChain` and update focused tests so reply-chain text remains visible but bot-sent media is not reattached as inbound media.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the current reply-chain media hydration behavior and are the strongest current-history owner for deciding whether that contract should change.
